Connections Recommended Power, Alarm, Grounding Wiring Scheme
LAN and Fiber Connection DC Power Connection
IGS-804SM-SE models have 8 electrical LAN ports (labeled 1~8) and 4 fiber ports A removable terminal block on the top panel provides both power and alarm
(SFP based, labeled Fiber 9~12) on the front panel. The LAN ports that utilize shielded connections. Power can be provided through the dual inputs from separate sources
RJ-45 connectors support 10/100/1000M; while the fiber SFP ports support (PWR1 & PWR2). One power supply is enough to power up the device. If two power
100/1000M. supplies are used, the device provides power redundancy function. See the figure
provided below for recommended DC power wiring scheme.
CONSOLE Port
The RJ-45 port labeled “CONSOLE” is an RS-232 terminal port for local management.
These models use a CLI (Command Line Interface) in addition to a user friendly Web
interface and industry standard SNMP. See page 6 for basic CLI and Web operation.
One RJ-45 to DB-9 cable is provided with this device. CONSOLE port pinouts and RS-
232 DB-9 connector are illustrated below together with RJ-45 to DB-9 signal mapping + - + -
information. Use the supplied cable to connect the RJ-45 CONSOLE port to a console
PC.

CLI & Web Basic Operation
Alarm Relay Connection
IGS-804SM-SE models are managed Gigabit Ethernet switch devices. Initial
The alarm relay contact can be wired into an alarm circuit which senses an
configuration (assignment of IP address) may be accomplished via the RS-232
alarm condition when the contact is broken. The alarm relay is normally closed
when there is no alarm condition. The alarm conditions are user console and a PC or laptop running terminal emulation software. Configure the
programmable through management to include power, link faults or other terminal as follows:
fault conditions. Please note that the alarm relay contact can only support 1A
115200 speed, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, no flow control
current at 24VDC. Do not apply voltage and current that exceed these
specifications. IGS-804SM-SE models use a command line interface (CLI) through the serial
port. Once the IP address has been configured, a web browser can be used to
configure the device through a more easy to use GUI (graphical user interface).
Please refer to the operation manual on the CDROM.
Using the provided console cable, connect the RJ-45 to the "CONSOLE" port
Normally Closed (NC)
and the DB9 to PC COM port. Apply power to the switch. At the "Username:"
prompt, enter 'admin' (lower case, no quotes). Just press Enter when
prompted for password.
To set the IP address and subnet mask, issue the following commands:
Fault
Example: sets VID 1 to 192.168.0.250, subnet 255.255.255.0)
Figure 8. Alarm Relay Wiring # config terminal
(config)# interface vlan 1
(config-if-vlan)# ip address 192.168.0.250 255.255.255.0
Earth Ground Connection
Then, press Enter.
An earth ground connector is provided on the top panel with an earth
ground sign next to it. Grounding the device can help to release leakage of NOTE: The factory default IP address is 10.1.1.1 with mask 255.255.255.0

interference (EMI).
